beats.ending_teaser: She got me fired — or so she thought — and then her own husband handed her the karma she deserved.
beats.backstory: I worked the customer service desk at a home goods store for three years. I was good at my job, never had a single complaint on my record. Then one Tuesday afternoon, a woman named Karen — I wish I was making that up — walked in with a lamp she clearly bought somewhere else.
beats.incident: The tag was from a completely different retailer. I told her politely we could not process the return. She lost it. Started screaming that I was calling her a liar, demanded my manager, and said she would have me fired before the day was over.
beats.escalation: My manager caved immediately and gave her store credit just to shut her up. But that was not enough. She filed a formal complaint saying I had been rude and aggressive — total fabrication. Corporate flagged my file and I was put on a written warning. Three years, spotless record, gone in an afternoon.
beats.resolution: Two weeks later she came back in to use that store credit. The man with her introduced himself to my manager as her husband — who also happened to be a regional loss prevention officer for our company. He had seen the security footage. She was banned on the spot and the complaint was wiped from my file.
beats.cta: Drop a comment telling me what you would have done differently. And follow for more stories like this one.
